headline: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, himself an immigrant from Taiwan, said the US should welcome the world's top talent, a view that clashes with the Trump administration's crackdown on skilled visas.
score_reason: A major tech leader, usually a Trump ally, publicly contradicts White House visa policy; it is a podcast remark, not a policy change.
importance_line: Skilled foreign workers and the US companies that hire them are affected by the visa fight, but this is a comment from one CEO and the White House has not shifted.
summary: Business Insider reports that Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia, said on the Bg2 podcast, "We want all the world's great minds to come here", while adding that immigrants must enter lawfully. The remarks cut against the Trump administration's curbs on H-1B visas (the main work visa for skilled foreigners), including a $100,000 fee for new applications; a White House spokeswoman told Business Insider the administration wants to prioritise American workers.
notes: Full text from fulltext file. Podcast date not stated; BI calls it 'recent'. It reacts to the administration's visa policy generally, including Vance's 8 Oct ban on Microsoft and Adobe from the green-card programme, but does not name a single earlier story.
